name: Independent on Sunday cryptic crossword No 1,553

clue.text: Bird losing argument in fight

indicators.note: losing something means doing without it, so the bird's name has those letters taken away

blocks.note: a common small brown bird
a row is a noisy quarrel

explanation.surface: A bird gives up a squabble rather than come to blows.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove ROW from SPARROW and SPAR is left.
explanation.definitionFit: To spar is to box or exchange blows, especially in practice, a milder sort of fighting.

clue.text: Landlady welcoming foreign lad holding tip of French stick

indicators.note: a host welcoming guests takes them inside, so the other letters go within
foreign suggests something made strange or unfamiliar, so the letters are rearranged
holding something means having it inside, so one letter is placed within the jumbled pair
the tip of a word is its very first letter, so only that one is kept

blocks.note: a host keeps guests, as a landlady keeps lodgers
taken as written, then mixed up
first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A landlady puts up a lad from abroad who is carrying a French loaf.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'stick' as a verb, not a loaf: the answer is the phrase HOLD FAST. A landlady is a host to her lodgers.
explanation.definitionFit: To hold fast is to cling firmly and refuse to let go, which is what sticking to something means.

clue.text: Relaxed alone prior to meeting with leader of supposed inferiors

indicators.note: something relaxed has loosened its fixed shape, so the letters fall into a new order
the leader of a word is whatever comes at its front, its opening letter

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written
first letter of the word

explanation.surface: Someone at ease alone before a meeting with the boss of those thought to be beneath them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prior to' reads like a phrase meaning before, but both words are part of the letters to be shuffled.
explanation.definitionFit: Poor relations are people or things regarded as lesser members of a group, looked down on by the rest.

clue.text: Saint sent abridged papal document to Byzantium

indicators.note: sent in the sense of carried away or sent flying, so the word's letters are thrown into a new order
an abridged text has been shortened, so the last letter is cut off

blocks.note: the letters of saint rearranged
a bull is a formal edict issued by the Pope

explanation.surface: A saint posts a shortened papal letter to the old Byzantine capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sent' looks like the verb of posting, but it means carried away, which signals the shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: Byzantium was the ancient Greek name of the city later called Constantinople and now known as Istanbul.

clue.text: Large queue turning up to receive tons of basic foodstuff

indicators.note: in a down clue turning up means reading from the bottom, so the queue word runs backwards
receiving something means taking it in, so a letter goes inside

blocks.note: L is the standard abbreviation for large
a line of people waiting
T is the abbreviation for ton or tons

explanation.surface: A big queue forms for tonnes of a staple food, as in a famine.
explanation.definitionFit: Lentils are dried pulses eaten as a cheap staple across much of the world.

clue.text: Advertising for irreligious lawyer?

blocks.note: pro is Latin for in favour of
a pagan follows no mainstream religion
DA is a District Attorney, a US prosecuting lawyer

explanation.surface: A cheeky question: is there any promotional material in favour of an unbelieving attorney?
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that 'Advertising' is a loose definition: propaganda is promotion of a cause rather than strictly advertising.
explanation.definitionFit: Propaganda is material spread to promote a cause or viewpoint, a kind of publicity or advertising.

clue.text: Policeman from the south is Scandinavian

indicators.note: in a down clue, reading from the south means reading upwards from the bottom, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: split as Police plus man: CID is the Criminal Investigation Department of a British police force, and Ron is a man's name

explanation.surface: A police officer who has come up from the south claims to be Scandinavian.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Policeman' looks like one word for an officer, but it must be split in two, and the result is read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Nordic describes the peoples and countries of northern Europe, including Scandinavia.

clue.text: Border held by determined Germans

indicators.note: held by means contained within, so the letters sit inside the following words

blocks.note: the end of determined and the start of Germans

explanation.surface: A frontier is defended by resolute Germans.
explanation.definitionFit: An edge is the outer limit or margin of something, the same as its border.

clue.text: Retired principal keeping hands over picture

indicators.note: retired means withdrawn or gone back, so the word is read backwards
keeping something means holding it inside, so a letter goes within

blocks.note: top means chief or principal
H is the abbreviation for hand, as in a farm hand
O is the cricket scoring abbreviation for an over

explanation.surface: A retired headteacher keeps handing over a picture.
explanation.definitionFit: A photo is a photograph, a picture taken with a camera.

clue.text: Foil covering display of bad language

definitions.note: bad language is a mass noun; the answer is one example of it

indicators.note: something covering another wraps around it, so one word goes inside the other

blocks.note: a foil is a light fencing sword
to wear a smile or a frown is to display it

explanation.surface: A sheet of foil is used to hide an offensive display.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Foil' suggests kitchen foil, but it is the fencer's sword, which goes around WEAR after its S: S-WEAR-WORD.
explanation.definitionFit: A swearword is a single obscene or profane word, an instance of bad language.

clue.text: Confused rat breeds with bird!

indicators.note: confused means mixed up, so the letters are jumbled into another order

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A muddled rodent attempts to mate with a bird, absurdly.
explanation.definitionFit: Redbreast is an old name for the robin, a small bird with an orange-red chest.

clue.text: Army chaplain has accommodation next to soldiers

indicators.note: next to means placed alongside, so one piece follows directly after the other

blocks.note: a pad is informal for a flat or home
RE is the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps

explanation.surface: The regimental chaplain is billeted beside the troops.
explanation.definitionFit: Padre is the informal title for a chaplain serving in the armed forces.

clue.text: Babe upset about rattle coming unstuck starts to get a little grizzly

indicators.note: upset means knocked over and disordered, so the letters are rearranged
about means around, so the rearranged word wraps the other letters
starts are beginnings, so only the opening letter of each word is used

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged
first letters of the three words

explanation.surface: A baby upset that its rattle has broken starts to get a little grumpy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grizzly' looks like the word for a whining child, which suits the babe, but here it is the bear.
explanation.definitionFit: Young bears are called cubs, so a small, immature grizzly is one of these youngsters.

clue.text: Financial middleman almost bankrupt

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped

blocks.note: a broker buys and sells on behalf of clients

explanation.surface: A stockbroker who is nearly ruined.
explanation.definitionFit: Broke is informal for having no money at all, penniless or ruined.

clue.text: Man eating guts of putrefied fish is a skinflint

indicators.note: eating something takes it inside, so a letter goes within the word for man
guts are innards, so the central letter of the word is taken

blocks.note: chap is informal for a man
middle letter of the nine-letter word
a skate is a flat ray-like sea fish

explanation.surface: Someone who eats rotten fish innards must be very mean with money.
explanation.definitionFit: A cheapskate is a stingy person who hates spending, just like a miser or skinflint.

clue.text: Sound made by soldier in pub

indicators.note: in places one item inside another, so the soldier sits within the pub

blocks.note: your local is the pub you regularly drink at
a GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: A noise is made by a soldier drinking in a bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound' looks like a noise, but it is the adjective, as in a sound argument.
explanation.definitionFit: A sound argument is valid and well reasoned, which is what logical means.

clue.text: Large port is charged

blocks.note: L is the abbreviation for large
Aden is a port city in Yemen

explanation.surface: A large harbour city is billed for its services.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charged' suggests a fee or an electrical charge, but here it means loaded.
explanation.definitionFit: Laden means loaded or burdened, as a ship charged with cargo is.

clue.text: See 31
See 31
Insignificant fluid loss?

definitions.note: a noun phrase; the answer is the gerund of the verb

blocks.note: first meaning: trivial or very small
second meaning, slangy and signalled by the question mark: passing water

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark warns that the second definition is playful: a loss of fluid is a trip to relieve oneself.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both an adjective for something trifling and the gerund of an informal verb for urinating.

clue.text: Spied for heads of national organisation, scrutinising every document

indicators.note: the heads of words are their first letters, so only those are kept

blocks.note: first letters of the five words

explanation.surface: An agent spied for the leaders of a national body that checks every paper.
explanation.definitionFit: To nose around is to pry or snoop, much as a spy does.

clue.text: Stays for two drinks before end of festivities

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, so only that one is kept

blocks.note: sup is a drink or sip, and port is a fortified wine
last letter of the word

explanation.surface: Someone lingers for a couple of drinks before the party ends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stays' looks like a verb about lingering, but it is a plural noun: props or braces.
explanation.definitionFit: Stays are props or braces, such as a ship's ropes or corset bones, that hold something up.

clue.text: Power given to the French after test case

indicators.note: after places the first pieces later in the word, following the next one

blocks.note: an exam is a test
P is the abbreviation for power in physics
le is a French word for the

explanation.surface: Authority is handed to the French after a legal test case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Test case' reads as a single legal phrase, but test is wordplay and case is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An example is an instance or case that illustrates something more general.

clue.text: Summary found in newspaper cutting

indicators.note: found in means located inside, so the letters are contained in the next words

blocks.note: the end of newspaper and the start of cutting

explanation.surface: A short summary turns up in a press clipping.
explanation.definitionFit: An aperçu is a brief outline or quick survey of a subject, borrowed from French.

clue.text: Recorded observations originally left in spaces in registers

indicators.note: originally means at the beginning, so the first letter of each word is taken
in places these letters inside the word for spaces

blocks.note: an en is a printer's unit of space
first letters of the two words
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: Notes once written down were left in the blank spaces of the records.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Registers' looks like a noun, but here it is a verb; an en is a printing measure half the width of an em.
explanation.definitionFit: To enrol is to put a name on an official list, signing up just as one registers.

clue.text: College fellow holding fragments of pad that's hard to decipher

indicators.note: holding something keeps it inside, so the shuffled letters go within
fragments are broken pieces, so the word is smashed and put back together differently

blocks.note: a dean is a senior fellow in a college
taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A don clutches scraps of a notepad covered in illegible writing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hard to decipher' suggests bad handwriting, but it describes an unreadable expression.
explanation.definitionFit: A deadpan face shows no emotion, so it is impossible to read, like an inscrutable poker face.

clue.text: European garlic's beginning to pong!

indicators.note: a word's beginning is its first letter, so just that one is kept

blocks.note: first letter of the word
pong is British slang for a bad smell, and to reek is to stink

explanation.surface: A European notices the garlic beginning to smell.
explanation.definitionFit: A Greek is a native of Greece, a country in southern Europe.

clue.text: See 31
See 3
Relative with endless string ...

indicators.note: endless means without an end, so the final letter is removed

blocks.note: twine is strong thin string

explanation.surface: A family member is holding an endless ball of string, continuing into the next clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A twin is a sibling born at the same birth, so a close family member.

clue.text: ... killed a great number

blocks.note: first meaning: past tense of slay
second meaning: a large quantity, as in a whole lot

explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links this to the previous clue so that a relative seems to have murdered many people with string.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is the past tense of slay and also an informal noun meaning a large amount or many.

clue.text: Cook latched on to competition involving various disciplines

indicators.note: to cook is to doctor or rework, so the letters are mixed into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A chef gets hooked on a multi-sport contest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cook' looks like a person, but it is the verb meaning to falsify, signalling the shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: A decathlon is an athletics contest of ten different track and field events.

clue.text: Restructuring helped things afoot beyond human control

annotation.answer: IN THE LAP OF THE GODS

indicators.note: restructuring means rebuilding in a different form, so the letters are reordered

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A reorganisation helped things already under way that nobody could influence.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom says an outcome rests with fate or chance, so no person can influence it.
